text:
marta (sec-eng): cloud-monitor alert: discovered S3 public-read on bucket `redwood-tfstate-backups-prod-1`. Objects include `prod.tfstate`, `prod.tfstate.backup`, and `secrets-archive.tar.gz`. Possible TF state leak. @alex (oncall) can you take containment?

alex (oncall): ack. I'll block public access and snapshot current ACL/policy. Creating incident channel now.

samir (infra): if tfstate includes IAM creds/ARNs we should assume keys could be used. I'll start searching CloudTrail for suspicious GET/PutObject calls.

alex (oncall): running containment commands now:
```
aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket redwood-tfstate-backups-prod-1 --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true
aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket redwood-tfstate-backups-prod-1 --policy file://deny-all-public.json
```
I'll keep a copy of the prior policy in /tmp/redwood-tfstate-backups-prod-1.policy.json before change.

jena (platform): pulling the tfstate to grep for access keys/service-account emails. If we find creds we need immediate rotation and session revocation.

security-bot: automated finding: 4 objects flagged with unusual last-modifier `ci-deploy-bot`. Recommend rotating any keys created in last 30 days and reviewing build artifacts. :rotating_light: 

samir (infra): CloudTrail shows a GETObject from 52.14.23.11 at 2026-03-20T03:12:14Z. IP geo unknown. Adding to denylist and creating firewall rule to block outgoing to that host.

alex (oncall): public access blocked and deny policy applied. Also invalidated pre-signed URLs referenced by pipeline (SSM). Next steps: rotate any keys found in tfstate, revoke STS sessions created by those keys. Assignments: @jena rotate creds, @samir investigate access logs + hunt for lateral activity, @marta lead post-incident.

marta (sec-eng): immediate mitigations performed: 1) public read blocked 2) CI deploy role creds rotated 3) forced logout for sessions tied to rotated keys 4) compliance/legal notified to evaluate disclosure obligations 5) started retention hold on bucket objects (snapshot to internal archive).

jena (platform): found AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and SECRET_KEY for user `tf-deployer` in `prod.tfstate`. Rotating now: creating new access key, updating pipeline secret store, invalidating old key. Also proposing wrapping tfstate with a customer-managed KMS key limited to infra roles only.

samir (infra): running org-wide inventory: `aws s3control list-public-access-block --account-id <id>` and `aws s3api get-bucket-acl --bucket <name>` across accounts to catch other misconfigs. Also kicking off terraform graph check to flag `acl = "public-read"` in repos.

alex (oncall): short comms: internal-only notice drafted for execs + CS ops. No customer PII confirmed yet; we'll escalate to legal if we find any. Creating incident channel `#inc-1818000000-terraform-tfstate-public`.

marta (sec-eng): proposed post-incident actions (owners):
- Add pre-commit/CI linter to block `acl = "public-read"` and `force_destroy=true` on state buckets (owner: eng-platform)
- Migrate remote state to private S3 endpoints (VPC endpoint) and require `kms:Decrypt` limited to infra roles (owner: platform)
- Enable CloudTrail data events for S3 on all tfstate buckets (owner: infra)
- Alert rule for any S3 object ACL==public-read or BucketPolicy allowing `Principal: *` (owner: sec-eng)
- Add automated scan to nightly job to detect tfstate files containing `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` patterns (owner: infra)

jena (platform): KMS plan: rotate CMK used by state, tighten key policy to only allow kms:Decrypt for `infra/terraform` role, and schedule key rotation. Will open PR for key policy change.

samir (infra): filed GH issue `infra/issue-4234` with remediation checklist and tests to prevent recurrence. Adding CI acceptance test to fail if tfstate artifacts are found in S3 backups.

alex (oncall): pausing pipeline `tfstate-backup` and blocking further scheduled backups until config is fixed. deploy-bot: paused pipeline `tfstate-backup`.

marta (sec-eng): scheduling postmortem for tomorrow 14:00 PST. We'll use the incident channel for updates, and I want a short write-up in 48h covering root cause, blast radius, and follow-ups.

jena (platform): quick note: might be caused by a new terraform module that defaulted `acl = "public-read"` for legacy reasons. We'll audit module defaults.

marta (sec-eng): thanks all. keep updates in #inc-1818000000-terraform-tfstate-public. Close this slack thread once all keys rotated and inventory clean.
